reason:
Measured across all fourteen states at 390/700/701/768/1152/1440. The numbers the finding reports are right; every inference it draws from them is wrong.

1. The artifact's responsive type policy is explicit, and .b-unit is on the correct side of it. Diffing every element of the horizon between 390 and 1440 on owner-flight: FOUR things step at 701 - .b-num 96->148, .b-when 20->30, .b-title 17->24, .b-away 15->17. EIGHT things are flat by design - .b-who 12, .b-unit 11, .b-sub 15, .b-todayLabel 11, .b-measureHead 11, .b-date 11, .b-where 11, .b-gapNote 15. The display/reading tier grades with the stage; the micro/data tier is a fixed anchor at every width. That is not an omission, it is the rule the file states at b.css:1275 ('Everything above is the phone. These are the only rules that raise it'). The finding asks to make .b-unit the single micro-tier element in the entire artifact that steps at 701 - a one-off exception to a policy held without a break in eight places. That is less system, not more.

2. The premise is factually wrong on the count size it names first. 'The count is drawn at three sizes... and the word that gives the figure its meaning has one size, 11px.' On the unfurl card the 64px count is .b-ogNum and its unit line is .b-ogDate - measured 15px GEIST, not 11px mono, reading 'days away when this was sent' (render-b.js:1581-1582, b.css:1094). Ratio there is 4.3:1. So the unit relationship is already 4.3 / 8.7 / 13.5 across the three count sizes; the finding omits the one that would have shown it, then reports the omission as the defect.

3. The fix does not solve the problem the finding states. The stated fault is 'the same relationship drawn at two very different proportions', 8.7:1 against 13.5:1. Injected the exact proposed rule and re-measured: the desk/print ratio becomes 148/13 = 11.4:1 while the phone stays 8.7:1. It closes 44% of the gap it names and replaces a two-value divergence with a three-value one (4.3 / 8.7 / 11.4). A fix that half-answers its own argument is not a 9.5-bar improvement.

4. Nothing visible changes on the flagship screen. Measured at 1440 owner-flight: 'days' goes from 28.2 x 15.4px to 33.3 x 19.5px beside a 165.8px numeral. Zero layout movement - .b-count 344 x 133.2 identical, .b-when top identical at 412.9, .b-todayRule identical at 506.4, document height identical at 1007. Before/after crops are all but indistinguishable. If 'at 148px days hangs off the corner as a footnote' is the defect, +2px does not cure it; if it is not, there is nothing here.

5. It re-fights a ratified round-6 decision and mischaracterises it twice. The confirmed micro-label-monoculture fix named .b-unit BY NAME and moved it into the DATA role - 'sentence case, --track-data, fore-72', the spec .b-away ships - which is exactly what renders: text-transform none, 0.44px (0.04em), rgba(...,0.72), lowercase 'days'. So the brief's framing of 'a small uppercase label' and the finding's 'same 11px step as Sat 1 Aug' both describe the fix, not a fault: the unit sits with the row date because a unit of measure IS data, and the whole point of that round was to stop the sub-15px tier being one undifferentiated object. Stepping 'days' to 13px puts it one size above 'Sat 1 Aug' inside the same role and splits the tier round 6 paid to consolidate. The round-6 letterfit analogy does not transfer either: tracking had to be size-graded because a flat -0.045em put o and d in 0.6px contact at 96px - a measured collision. There is no analogous failure at 11px.

6. The fix makes the keepsake worse, and it is scoped to hit it. [data-medium="sheet"] is what the printed sheet carries, so the rule lands on print. On the A4 preview at 1152 and 1440 the unit is not 'days' - it is 'days away on Thursday 16 July 2026' set three lines into the numeral's shoulder. Injected: the stack grows 84.5 x 46.2 -> 99.8 x 58.5, the left column and the ceremonial date drop 9.3px, the sheet grows 971.9 -> 981.3px, and the unit box goes from clearing the right track by 5.2px (right 490.8, column 2 at 496) to crossing it by 10.2px (right 506.2). No ink collides yet, but the only clearance the two tracks have is consumed and inverted, and the A/B crop shows the discreet caption becoming a dense mono block competing with the 30px date under it. Round 7 refuted a finding against this exact stack on the grounds that it 'reads cleanly as a deliberate stack tucked into the numeral's shoulder'; enlarging it 18% works against that verdict.

7. What is left is a ratio, and this panel has already ruled on ratios. Round 8: 'do not assert away strictly smaller than title - that is a ratio, and a ratio is taste.' Nothing renders wrong. Baselines are identical to 0.00px in every state and at every width I probed with a zero-height strut (phone 237.58/237.58, desk 264.19/264.19, print 264.19/264.19), contrast passes, no wrap, no overlap, no clipping. The finding's own gate diligence is sound - I confirmed Geist Mono|13|body already holds lead 1.5 and track 0.04em on .b-printLinkUrl, so the rule is gate-neutral across all fourteen states - but a change that is invisible on screen, unhelpful to the problem it names, contrary to a stated size policy and harmful on paper does not become worth making just because the gates would stay green. Minor: the finding cites b.css:192-196 for .b-unit; that is .b-away. .b-unit is b.css:76-82.
sharpenedFix: Nothing to do. Leave .b-unit at --size-label; it is one of eight micro/data-tier elements the artifact deliberately holds flat across the 701 breakpoint, and it is where the confirmed round-6 data-role fix put it. If a future round still wants the count's satellite to feel less like a footnote at 148px, the lever is NOT font-size - +2px is invisible - and it must not be applied under [data-medium="sheet"], because on the sheet the same element carries a three-line dated clause with only 5.2px of clearance from the right track. The only change worth testing would be ink, not size: .b-unit at fore (100%) rather than fore-72 on the desk horizon only, which costs no layout, no ramp step and no gate, and actually addresses the complaint that the unit reads as a footnote. Test it against the round-6 data-role ink ladder before proposing it - fore-72 is that ladder's data step, so raising it would need its own argument.
